rules: Keep hook policy canonical in-repo and project it outward.
Preserve unrelated agent-native settings; only managed hook events are rewritten.
Use one shared checkpoint + post-write consensus path before inventing per-client variants.
Prefer non-blocking observability and cheap background consensus over prompt-time token burn.

hermes_user.reason: This is the REAL Hermes home -- where the gateway actually runs and where Hermes reads its config -- not `.toilet/hermes/`, which is the operator's scratch document dump (gitignored) and was never the live gateway. The former `hermes_workspace` target (pointing at `.toilet/hermes/config.yaml`) has been removed entirely; this manifest no longer manages anything under `.toilet`. SessionStart is intentionally omitted -- it has no clean Hermes equivalent, so it is left unmapped rather than inventing one; the event_map mechanism drops any manifest event absent from it. `entry_shape: "flat"` is required because Hermes's own `agent/shell_hooks.py::_parse_single_entry` expects one flat `{matcher?, command}` mapping per hook, not the Claude-Code-nested `{matcher, hooks: [{type, command}]}` shape the other targets use -- the nested shape parsed to zero hooks (warn-and-skip on the missing `command` field) until this was fixed. The matcher is `write_file|patch` (Hermes's actual file-editing tool names -- confirmed against `tools/file_tools.py`), not `Write|Edit|MultiEdit`, which is Claude/Codex vocabulary Hermes tools never emit; `ShellHookSpec.matches_tool` fullmatches this as a regex against `tool_name`. This hook block matches, byte-for-byte, the hooks already present and allowlisted (`hermes hooks list` reports both ✓ allowed) in the live AppData config -- adopted as-is, not rewritten.
